Determine the Taylor number for Taylor-Couette flow between two concentric rotating cylinders.
The gap between the cylinders is 2 mm.
The inner cylinder has a radius of 50 mm and rotates at an angular velocity of 10π/3 rad/s (100 rpm).
The outer cylinder is stationary (angular velocity = 0).
The outer cylinder radius is 52 mm (inner radius plus gap).
The fluid has a kinematic viscosity of 1 × 10⁻⁵ m²/s (derived from dynamic viscosity μ = 0.01 Pa·s and density ρ = 1000 kg/m³).
Compute the Taylor number using the standard definition Ta = (R_i · Ω_i · d / ν)² · (1 − 1/η²), where η = R_o / R_i, R_i is the inner radius, R_o is the outer radius, Ω_i is the inner angular velocity, d is the gap, and ν is the kinematic viscosity.
Report the final numerical value of the Taylor number.
